construct: Carbon monoxide forms carboxyhemoglobin, reducing hemoglobin oxygen-carrying capacity and increasing the oxygen affinity of remaining unoccupied heme sites, producing a left shift in the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve while dissolved arterial oxygen tension may remain normal.

notes: Current USMLE Step 1 Exam Content verified 2026-09-01; Tables 1–3.
Carbon Monoxide Poisoning — StatPearls current record; Pathophysiology supports carboxyhemoglobin, reduced oxygen capacity, left shift and tissue hypoxia.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Normal PaO2 means dissolved oxygen can be preserved. CO impairs oxygen delivery by occupying hemoglobin and making remaining sites hold oxygen more tightly, so oxygen content and unloading fall despite normal dissolved oxygen tension.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Carbon monoxide can also impair mitochondrial respiration, but the question asks why severe tissue hypoxia can coexist with normal PaO2. The uniquely direct explanation is reduced hemoglobin oxygen capacity plus left-shifted unloading; PaO2 measures dissolved oxygen.
